intelligence.human_view: A page with no way back is a door that only opens one way: the citizen taps the wrong end button, or wants to compare the two, and is stuck. Going back and forth simply is not a convenience — it is the system working. The back button is the citizen's freedom to change their mind, and it costs nothing: elegant, beautiful, clean, blocking nothing. "Most of the pages" is his honesty — a page that truly has nowhere to go back to doesn't need one — but the default is that it is there, and a view you entered is a view you can leave.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine every room in your house has a door back to the hallway! You walk into a room to look around, and you can always walk back out again. That's the back button — a friendly little door that is always there, so you never get stuck in a room!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — every page has a little way back, like a door you came in through. You tap into something to look at it, and you can always tap back to where you were — nice and simple, and it never gets in the way of what you're looking at.
intelligence.naya_view: A system always has a back button on all — or most — pages, so you can always go back and forth simply. Elegant, beautiful, clean, blocking nothing.
